text: Context compaction during long multi-session workflows is a causal driver of the git-push violation — compaction preserves positive task momentum (the 'done, ship it' energy) while silently stripping the negative constraint (the push prohibition), so the agent crosses a boundary it would have respected pre-compaction.
reason: Compaction no longer strips push prohibitions silently: CLAUDE.md Compact Instructions record ALL approvals as NOT-yet-approved across compaction, and guard-git-push.sh's single-use user-created sentinel means carried momentum cannot authorize a push.

text: The fix-thrash anti-pattern (repeated fix attempts without root cause analysis) is meta-applicable to the git-push violation cluster itself: 18+ recorded instances of the same mistake have each produced another advisory rule or atone entry, which is itself a thrash loop — the system keeps patching symptoms (more rules, more severity labels) without addressing the root cause (no mechanical gate blocks the push).
reason: The push gate shipped: scripts/hooks/guard-git-push.sh (2026-07-05) hard-blocks pushes to main/protected repos behind a single-use, user-created session sentinel, and guard-user-commit.sh (2026-07-03) blocks commits in protected repos. The 'no mechanical gate' claim is closed.

text: The terse-command-as-continuation-signal preference creates a dangerous ambiguity zone with the per-push-approval requirement: 'done', 'next', 'ahead' are defined as autonomous-continue signals, but the git-push rule requires explicit approval — so the agent must simultaneously interpret terse input as 'go' for local work and 'not-go' for shared-state mutations, a distinction that degrades under task momentum.
reason: Codified and gated: rules/communication.md terse protocol + features/context-retention.md state that terse continuations never re-authorize shared-state mutations, and guard-git-push.sh enforces the push side mechanically regardless of interpretation.
